_comment: The gate treats 'zero failures' as success, so a run that silently skips tests
reports PASS having tested less than it should have. Skips are how this suite
degrades when content or Stache state is unavailable (#1738, #1740), which is
deliberate — but it makes coverage loss invisible. These counts make an
unexpected skip a failure instead of silence.
Raising a number here is a deliberate, reviewable act. If a band exceeds its
baseline, the default assumption is a real regression — a starved worker, a
missing content submodule, a guard firing on a lookup that should have
resolved. Update the baseline only once you know why the new skip is correct,
and say so in the PR.

Windows.why: Measured on the windows-latest band of run 41364357633 (#348). Thirteen cases cannot run on Windows and carry skipOnWindows: twelve in WatchUpstreamWorkflowTest, which runs the upstream watcher against a POSIX stub, and the symlink case in DeclinedBoostSkillsTest. Linux and macOS run all thirteen, so the shared number stays 3 and they stay covered there.

parallel.why: Two SchemaThingFromRelationship cases skip on a missing subject_matter::cellulitis term. One StoredSvgHazardScanTest case skips because CI checks out only the content/ and users/ submodules, not the binary-heavy public/assets one it scans (#1739) — the scanner's own detection logic is covered unconditionally by tests/Unit/Support/Imaging/SvgHazardScannerTest.php, so only the corpus sweep depends on that submodule. The three RegistrantRecordsAreGitIgnoredTest cases are deliberately NOT in this count: both gates check out the users/ submodule since #2477, so they run, and a gate that stops checking it out shows up here as three unexpected skips rather than as a silent pass.

serial.why: The serial tail runs with content present and skips nothing.
